投資與評價 
1. 頎邦 3Q26 受惠美系手機新機備貨 ， 加上1.6T 光通訊 TIA 與 PD 訂單放
量，推升營收及毛利率；預期 4Q26 手機 DDIC 相關需求季節性放緩，
惟光通訊訂單持續成長，Modulator 量產及 TFLN 新案導入支撐營運。 
2. 頎邦 26 年受惠光通訊金凸塊訂單放量，EPS 6.03 元；27 年 1.6T 光通
訊需求成長，TFLN 量產與測試業務擴張，光通訊相關營收佔比達兩成，
加上韓系 DDIC 轉單挹注，推升營運，EPS 10.52 元。 
3. 目前頎邦股價交易在 226.0 元(21.5X 27(F) PER)，位於近三年參考本益
比區間 18~42x 區間下緣位置，考量頎邦在金凸塊製程具備技術與產能
優勢，加上測試與切割業務擴張有望提高單片晶圓加工產值，給予平均
值 30 倍本益比與強力買進投資建議 ， 目標價315.0 元(30X 27(F) PER)。 
重點更新 
頎邦 3Q26 光通訊與美系手機新機需求雙引擎帶動營運創近四年新高  
頎邦 3Q26 受惠於美系手機品牌大廠新機備貨需求帶動 OLED DDI 及 RF 相
關金凸塊業務成長，加上 AI 資料中心持續升級至 1.6T 光收發模組，帶動單
通道 200G 相關 TIA 及 PD 金凸塊需求增加，預估頎邦 3Q26 營收 75.82 億
元(+14.3% QoQ) 。高毛利率的光通訊業務營收占比提升， 且整體產能利用
率改善，預估毛利率 31.9%(+1.6ppts QoQ)。光通訊新產品開發、測試技術
導入費用增加，預估營業利益 16.41 億元(+28.4% QoQ) ，稅後淨利 15.56
億元(+63.8% QoQ)，EPS 2.10 元，營運創近四年新高。 
預期頎邦 4Q26 DDIC 需求季節性放緩，光通訊與 TFLN 新業務支撐營運 
頎邦 4Q26 OLED DDI 及 RF 相關需求季節性放緩 ， 惟光通訊業務持續受惠於
200G/lane 金凸塊需求成長，加上國內晶圓代工大廠旗下的特殊製程業者
TFLN 預計於 4Q26 開始貢獻六吋 ， 國內晶圓代工大廠八吋TFLN 也將開始貢
獻，且我們推測 TFLN 從金凸塊到 Testing、Dicing 都會交給頎邦，故 ASP
會大幅提高。預估頎邦 4Q26 營收 75.02 億元(-1.1% QoQ) 。雖光通訊營收
占比提升但 DDIC 產能利用率因季節性需求放緩而下降，加上新產品導入初
期的相關成本，預估毛利率 31.4%(-0.6ppts QoQ)。隨光通訊測試及封裝相
關技術持續開發，且新產品認證及研發投入增加，預估營業費用為8.40 億元
(+7.7% QoQ)，稅後淨利 15.32 億元(-1.5% QoQ)，EPS 2.06 元。

報告內容 
頎邦 3Q26 光通訊與美系手機新機需求雙引擎帶動營運創近四年新高 
頎邦 3Q26 受惠於美系手機品牌大廠新機備貨需求帶動 OLED DDI 及 RF 相關金凸塊業務成長，
加上 AI 資料中心持續升級至 1.6T 光收發模組，帶動單通道 200G 相關 TIA 及 PD 金凸塊需求
增加，美系多家大客戶訂單持續放量，預估頎邦 3Q26 營收 75.82 億元(+14.3% QoQ) 。由於
頎邦 2Q26 針對 DDIC 客戶調漲加工價格的效益持續反映，且高毛利率的光通訊業務營收占比
提升，搭配整體產能利用率改善，八吋產能利用率由前一季之 70%提升至 75%，十二吋由前一
季之近 90%提升至 90%以上 ，預估毛利率 31.9%(+1.6ppts QoQ)。 隨光通訊相關新產品開發、
測試技術導入及人員費用增加 ， 預估營業費用為7.80 億元(+6.6% QoQ)， 營業利益16.41 億元
(+28.4% QoQ)。預估稅後淨利 15.57 億元(+63.9% QoQ)，EPS 2.10 元，營運創近四年新高。

預期頎邦 4Q26 傳統 DDIC 需求季節性放緩，光通訊與 TFLN 新業務支撐營運 
隨美系手機品牌大廠新機備貨高峰結束，OLED DDI 及 RF 相關需求季節性放緩，加上 TV、
Monitor 及 NB 等傳統 DDIC 終端需求仍相對疲弱，惟光通訊業務持續受惠於200G/lane 金凸
塊需求成長，且美系客戶的 Modulator 預計自 4Q26 有望開始量產，其他多家美系客戶的 TIA
與 PD 既有訂單維持出貨，加上國內晶圓代工大廠旗下的特殊製程業者 TFLN 預計於 4Q26 開
始貢獻六吋，國內晶圓代工大廠八吋 TFLN 也將開始貢獻，兩者合計約 2,000 片左右，九成以
上的 TFLN 的設備都是使用既有的即可銜接上，頎邦六吋以及八吋都可以做，且我們推測 TFLN
從金凸塊到 Testing、Dicing 都會交給頎邦，故 ASP 會大幅提高。 
預估頎邦 4Q26 營收 75.02 億元(-1.0% QoQ) 。雖光通訊營收占比提升及 2Q26 價格調整效益
持續挹注，惟 DDIC 產能利用率因季節性需求放緩而下降，加上新產品導入初期的相關成本，
預估毛利率 31.4%(-0.5ppts QoQ)。隨光通訊測試及封裝相關技術持續開發，且新產品認證及
研發投入增加，預估營業費用為8.40 億元(+7.7% QoQ)，營業利益 15.12 億元(-7.9% QoQ)。
稅後淨利 15.33 億元(-1.5% QoQ)，EPS 2.06 元，光通訊與 TFLN 新業務支撐營運。

頎邦 26 年受惠光通訊業務加速放量與 DDIC 漲價，營運創近四年新高 
頎邦傳統 DDIC 業務受惠於韓系競爭對手逐步退出成熟封裝市場，產業供需結構改善，使公司
自 2Q26 起調漲部分 DDIC 後段加工價格，加上美系手機品牌大廠 OLED DDI 與 RF 相關需求
維持穩健，帶動既有業務營收回升。且隨 AI 資料中心由 800G 逐步升級至 1.6T 光收發模組，
單通道傳輸速度提升至 200G，使 TIA、PD、Driver 及 Modulator 對低損耗互連的需求增加，
帶動金凸塊逐步取代傳統打線封裝， 
預估 26 年光通訊相關營收約 16.31 億元，包含 TFLN 0.31 億元，占整體營收約 5.9%，全年營
收 274.72 億元(+28.1% YoY) 。受惠於 DDIC 加工價格調漲、產能利用率回升，以及毛利率較
高的光通訊業務占比提升，預估毛利率由 25 年之 21.4%提高至 29.6%(+8.2ppts YoY) 。隨公
司持續投入光通訊金凸塊、測試及切割等新製程開發，且營運規模擴大帶動人事及管理費用增
加，預估營業費用 29.14 億元(+33.0% YoY)，在價格調整及產品組合優化下，營業利益 52.19
億元(+117.5% YoY)，稅後淨利 44.77 億元(+61.3% YoY)，EPS 6.03 元，營運創近四年新高。

預期頎邦 27 年受惠韓系 DDIC 轉單與光通訊與 TFLN 業務加速放量，營運創歷史新高 
頎邦 27 年隨 AI 資料中心高速光互連需求持續成長，1.6T 光收發模組滲透率提升，帶動 TIA、
PD、Driver 及 Modulator 金凸塊訂單放量，其中包括美系客戶的 Driver 與 PIC 相關新案、另
一家的 TIA 也開始量產 ，及 4Q26 開始量產的 Modulator 預計陸續擴大營收貢獻 。TFLN 方面，
六吋及八吋相關產品預計逐步放量，頎邦可望承接金凸塊、測試及組裝等製程， 提供更完整的
一站式服務，進一步增加單片晶圓營收貢獻，預估 27 年光通訊相關營收約年增 4.5 倍至 72.68
億元，包括 15.68 億元的 TFLN，占整體營收約 20.1%。韓系廠商逐步退出面板 DDIC 相關生
產，預計八吋及十二吋在 27 年年底會完全退出，自 1Q27 起部分訂單轉由國內晶圓代工大廠
代工，頎邦有望承接後段金凸塊及封測需求，且隨 27 年底轉單逐步完成，將有助於傳統 DDIC
業務維持成長。 
預估 27 年營收 362.11 億元(+31.8% YoY)。 由於光通訊相關測試業務附加價值高於傳統金凸塊
製程，隨測試設備稼動率提升及高毛利產品營收占比增加，加上 DDIC 業務可能於 1Q27 再度
調漲加工價格，預估毛利率由 26 年之 29.6%再度提升至 34.8%(+5.2ppts YoY) 。隨公司擴大
測試設備投資，且新產品開發、設備折舊與相關人事費用增加，預估營業費用 40.32 億元
(+38.4% YoY)，惟營收規模擴大及產品組合改善帶動營業利益 85.84 億元(+64.5% YoY)，預估
稅後淨利 78.21 億元(+74.7% YoY)，EPS 10.52 元，營運歷史創新高。

產業簡介 
頎邦所處的半導體封裝測試(Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test, OSAT )位於晶
圓製造之後，主要負責晶圓凸塊、晶圓測試、切割、封裝及成品測試等後段製程。過去封測產
業主要隨半導體出貨量成長，但隨先進製程微縮難度提高、Chiplet 及異質整合普及，封裝已由
單純保護與電性連接功能，逐步成為影響系統效能、功耗及頻寬的重要環節。 
 
對頎邦而言，核心市場與一般以 CPU、GPU 先進封裝為主的 OSAT 不同，公司長期聚焦於
Display Driver IC(DDI)後段封裝測試。DDI 主要功能為將影像處理晶片輸出的數位訊號轉換為
面板像素所需的驅動訊號，廣泛應用於手機、電視、顯示器、Notebook 及車載面板。DDI 供
應鏈上游為 8 吋及 12 吋晶圓代工，中游為 IC 設計，後段則依序涉及 Gold Bumping 、Chip 
Probing、Grinding/Dicing，以及 COG、COF 或 COP 等封裝製程。 
 
DDI 具有成熟製程占比較高、終端需求與消費電子景氣連動、但先進顯示技術持續提升封裝規
格的產業特性。過去 DDI 大量採用 8 吋成熟製程，但近年部分高階 OLED DDI 逐步往 12 吋製
造發展；同時，全球成熟製程供給結構正在改變。 
 
終端需求方面，傳統 LCD 顯示市場已進入成熟期，整體 DDI 產業未來成長較難單純依賴終端
台數，而將更多來自OLED 滲透、解析度提升、高更新率、TDDI 整合及車載顯示等產品升級。

在封裝技術方面，Gold Bump 為 DDI 的重要互連製程，利用薄膜、黃光及電鍍在 IC Pad 上形
成金凸塊，再透過熱壓方式與外部電路連接。DDI 具有 Die 狹長、I/O 數量高及 Pitch 持續縮
小等特性，因此對 Bump 高度均勻性、Fine Pitch 及良率控制要求較高。後續封裝依終端應用
不同可分為 COG、COF 及 COP，其中 COG 直接將 IC 與玻璃基板連接，具封裝薄、高腳數密
度等優勢 ；COF 則將 Gold Bump 與柔性 Film 上的 Inner Lead 熱壓接合 ， 具可撓曲與Fine Pitch
優勢，目前已可支援小於 16μm 的 Super Fine Pitch ，為大尺寸 LCD/OLED 及多數 IT 面板的
重要封裝方案；COP 則利用可撓式塑膠基板將 Driver IC 彎折至 OLED 面板背面，主要應用於
窄邊框 Flexible OLED 手機。隨面板解析度、更新率及 I/O 數提升，對 Fine Pitch Gold Bump
與高精度封裝能力的要求亦同步提高。

除成熟 DDI 市場外 ， 高速光通訊正成為Gold Bump 產業新的結構性成長方向 。AI Data Center
持續擴大 GPU/XPU Cluster 規模，使運算節點之間的資料傳輸量與功耗快速增加，推動
Ethernet 光模組由 400G、800G 進一步升級至 1.6T，單 Lane 傳輸速率亦由 100G/lane 提升
至 200G/lane。 
 
高速化亦改變光模組內部封裝架構 。Broadcom 已推出支援 1.6T DR8/FR8 的 200G/lane PAM4 
PHY，Marvell 亦已量產 200G/lane TIA 與 Mach-Zehnder Modulator Driver 晶片組，反映
1.6T 世代正式進入 200G/lane。隨傳輸頻率提高，PD 至 TIA 以及 Driver 至 Modulator 之間
的 Electrical Path 越短越有利於降低寄生效應與訊號損耗，因此 Flip-Chip 及 Bump-based 
interconnect 的重要性提升 ，Gold Bump 的應用亦由傳統 DDI、RF 逐步延伸至 TIA、PD、Driver
及 Modulator 等高速光通訊元件。 
 
圖三. 金凸塊製程 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
資料來源: 國祥貿易、國泰證期研究部整理 
 
隨光通訊由單通道 100G 升級至 200G，訊號傳輸頻率提升，使傳統打線封裝因導線較長而產
生更明顯的寄生電感 、 訊號損耗及雜訊干擾 ， 因此高速光通訊晶片逐步導入金凸塊(Gold Bump)，
藉由縮短晶片間的電性連接距離，改善訊號完整性。接收端 (Rx)方面，光偵測器(PD)將接收到
的光訊號轉換為微弱電訊號，再由跨阻放大器(TIA)放大，由於訊號強度極低，PD 與 TIA 之間
須透過金凸塊縮短傳輸路徑，降低雜訊及訊號失真；發射端(Tx)方面，Driver 接收來自 DSP 的
高速電訊號，並驅動調變器 (Modulator)將電訊號轉換為光訊號的調變資訊，因此 Driver 與
Modulator 同樣需要低寄生效應的高速電性互連，以維持訊號品質。隨 1.6T 及 3.2T 光收發模
組逐步導入，金凸塊將由接收端 TIA、PD 延伸至發射端 Driver、Modulator，帶動光通訊金凸
塊需求及相關封裝產值持續提升。

公司簡介 
頎邦(6147.TT)成立於 1997 年，總部位於新竹科學園區，2002 年於櫃買中心掛牌，為台灣主
要半導體封裝測試廠之一，長期專注於顯示驅動 IC(Display Driver IC, DDI )後段製程。公司由
金凸塊(Gold Bumping)製程起家 ， 並逐步建立晶圓測試(Chip Probing, CP)、 晶圓研磨與切割、
COF(Chip on Film)、COG(Chip on Glass)、WLCSP 等完整封裝測試能力，是少數能提供 DDI
由凸塊、測試至後段封裝完整製程服務的廠商；公司官方將自身定位為全球最大顯示驅動IC 封
裝測試廠之一。頎邦目前於台灣設有新竹科學園區力行、展業、研發廠、新竹產業園區光復廠，
以及高雄南六、南一廠等生產據點，其中新竹主要負責 Bumping、Testing、Grinding/Dicing
及 Assembly，高雄則以測試、封裝及 COF T ape製造為主。 
 
頎邦核心技術為晶圓級凸塊製程，公司透過薄膜、黃光及電鍍製程，在晶片 Pad 上形成 Gold 
Bump，並進一步發展銅鎳金凸塊、RDL 等相關技術。金凸塊過去主要應用於 DDI，搭配 COF
或 COG 等 Flip-Chip 封裝，以滿足顯示驅動晶片高 I/O、Fine Pitch 及薄型化需求；目前公司
相關製程已可支援不同尺寸晶圓，且由傳統矽基晶圓延伸至 GaAs、GaN、SiC 及 LiT aO3等化
合物半導體材料。除封裝測試服務外，公司亦具備 Flexible Tape-and-Reel Circuit Substrate
及 Chip Tray 等產品，使其在 DDI 供應鏈涵蓋由凸塊、測試、封裝至部分材料與載具的垂直整
合能力。 
 
產品應用方面，頎邦過去高度集中於 DDI，但近年持續利用既有 Gold Bump 及 Wafer Test能
力拓展非驅動 IC 業務。依 2026 年公司法說資訊，DDI 目前仍約占營收 60–65%，主要應用於
手機、TV 與 NB/PC；RF Front-end 約占 20%，RFID 約占 3%，其餘則包含電源管理、化合物
半導體及其他新產品。相較過去 DDI 占比逾九成，公司產品組合已逐步朝 RF、RFID 及高附加
價值封裝應用分散，降低成熟顯示驅動 IC 市場對營運的單一影響。 
 
2026 年起，矽光子(Silicon Photonics )成為頎邦另一項重要新業務。隨 AI 資料中心光通訊由
100G/lane 升級至 200G/lane，PD、TIA、Driver 及 Modulator 等高速元件對短距離、高訊
號完整性的互連要求提高，部分架構由傳統 Wire Bond 轉向 Flip-Chip／Gold Bump，使頎邦
既有金凸塊技術開始由 DDI 延伸至高速光通訊。公司目前已切入TIA、Photodetector、Driver
及 Modulator 等元件 ， 其中部分產品已於2026 年量產 ， 並持續擴大相關客戶與專案 ； 截至2026
年第三季，DDI 仍占營收六成以上，但矽光業務已成為非 DDI 產品中成長最快的項目之一。 
 
在全球布局方面，頎邦除台灣既有生產基地外，近年亦因應客戶供應鏈在地化與地緣政治需求
擴大海外布局。公司 2026 年於馬來西亞檳城啟用新廠，投資規模約 US$200mn，主要目的為
增加海外生產彈性 、 滿足客戶Non-China/Non-T aiwan供應鏈需求並降低單一地區製造風險；
公司亦於 2025 年永續報告中明確將馬來西亞據點擴建列為強化全球產能配置與供應鏈韌性的
核心措施之一。

頎邦 ESG 政策 
頎邦(6147.TT)將永續發展納入公司治理及日常營運架構，ESG 政策主要涵蓋公司治理、環境永
續、員工與社會責任及供應鏈管理四大方向。公司依循《上市上櫃公司永續發展實務守則》及
責任商業聯盟行為準則(RBA Code of Conduct )等國內外規範訂定永續政策，核心原則包括健
全公司治理與資訊揭露、降低溫室氣體與資源消耗、保障勞動人權與職業安全，以及要求供應
鏈共同落實企業社會責任。治理架構方面，公司於董事會層級建立永續監督機制，並設有永續
發展指導委員會及永續發展執行委員會，下設公司治理、環境安全與供應鏈管理、員工權益關
懷、資訊安全及社會參與等功能小組，定期追蹤重大永續議題、溫室氣體盤查、IFRS S1/S2 導
入及各項年度 ESG 目標執行情形，再向董事會報告。 
 
環境面以降低製造端碳排、能源效率提升及再生能源導入為主要政策方向。 頎邦依 TCFD 架構
辨識氣候轉型及實體風險，並以 ISO 14064-1 進行溫室氣體盤查，盤查範圍目前涵蓋台灣六個
營運據點 ， 自2021 年起並導入第三方查證 。2025 年 Scope 1 與 Scope 2 合計排放量為 150,934
公噸 CO₂e，YoY 下降 2.36%，較 2021 基準年下降 11.89%，其中 Scope 2 電力相關排放占整
體排放 74.85%，顯示外購電力仍為主要減碳重點。公司設定 2026 年 Scope 1+2 較 2021 年
減少 12%、2030 年減少 23%，長期則配合台灣 2050 淨零路徑。 
 
能源管理方面，公司透過 ISO 50001 架構、設備汰換、機台操作優化及製程效率改善降低能源

承諾書簽署。衝突礦產方面，公司針對金、鎢、錫等材料進行冶煉廠溯源，2025 年調查 19 家
相關原物料及外包供應商，結果顯示相關材料 100%非來自衝突礦區。 
 
公司治理面則以董事會監督、風險管理、誠信經營及資訊安全為主軸。 頎邦目前董事會共有 6
席董事，其中 3 席為獨立董事，並設置審計、薪資報酬、提名及永續發展指導委員會；永續發
展指導委員會於 2025 年 7 月成立，負責協助董事會規劃 ESG 政策、目標並督導執行情形。公
司亦於 2024 年將風險管理小組改隸由全體獨立董事組成的審計委員會，提高風險管理與董事
會監督連結；薪酬制度則將財務及非財務 ESG 績效納入董事與經理人績效及薪酬考量。 
 
在資安方面，公司以 ISO 27001 建立資訊安全管理體系，2025 年維持 ISO 27001:2022 驗證
有效性，並執行社交工程演練、教育訓練及營業秘密保護課程，全年無重大資安事件；未來目
標為維持重大資安事件零發生、郵件社交工程演練涵蓋率100%，並將上鉤率控制於 5%以下。
此外，頎邦已連續十二屆位列公司治理評鑑上櫃公司前 5%，反映其公司治理制度與資訊揭露
機制已具一定成熟度。

產業簡介
頎邦所處的半導體封裝測試(Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test, OSAT )位於晶
圓製造之後，主要負責晶圓凸塊、晶圓測試、切割、封裝及成品測試等後段製程。過去封測產
業主要隨半導體出貨量成長，但隨先進製程微縮難度提高、Chiplet 及異質整合普及，封裝已由
單純保護與電性連接功能，逐步成為影響系統效能、功耗及頻寬的重要環節。

對頎邦而言，核心市場與一般以 CPU、GPU 先進封裝為主的 OSAT 不同，公司長期聚焦於
Display Driver IC(DDI)後段封裝測試。DDI 主要功能為將影像處理晶片輸出的數位訊號轉換為
面板像素所需的驅動訊號，廣泛應用於手機、電視、顯示器、Notebook 及車載面板。DDI 供
應鏈上游為 8 吋及 12 吋晶圓代工，中游為 IC 設計，後段則依序涉及 Gold Bumping 、Chip
Probing、Grinding/Dicing，以及 COG、COF 或 COP 等封裝製程。

DDI 具有成熟製程占比較高、終端需求與消費電子景氣連動、但先進顯示技術持續提升封裝規
格的產業特性。過去 DDI 大量採用 8 吋成熟製程，但近年部分高階 OLED DDI 逐步往 12 吋製
造發展；同時，全球成熟製程供給結構正在改變。

終端需求方面，傳統 LCD 顯示市場已進入成熟期，整體 DDI 產業未來成長較難單純依賴終端
台數，而將更多來自OLED 滲透、解析度提升、高更新率、TDDI 整合及車載顯示等產品升級。

圖二. Semiconductor wafer manufacturing to packaging and testing

資料來源: Mazak、國泰證期研究部整理

在封裝技術方面，Gold Bump 為 DDI 的重要互連製程，利用薄膜、黃光及電鍍在 IC Pad 上形
成金凸塊，再透過熱壓方式與外部電路連接。DDI 具有 Die 狹長、I/O 數量高及 Pitch 持續縮
小等特性，因此對 Bump 高度均勻性、Fine Pitch 及良率控制要求較高。後續封裝依終端應用
不同可分為 COG、COF 及 COP，其中 COG 直接將 IC 與玻璃基板連接，具封裝薄、高腳數密
度等優勢 ；COF 則將 Gold Bump 與柔性 Film 上的 Inner Lead 熱壓接合 ， 具可撓曲與Fine Pitch
優勢，目前已可支援小於 16μm 的 Super Fine Pitch ，為大尺寸 LCD/OLED 及多數 IT 面板的
重要封裝方案；COP 則利用可撓式塑膠基板將 Driver IC 彎折至 OLED 面板背面，主要應用於
窄邊框 Flexible OLED 手機。隨面板解析度、更新率及 I/O 數提升，對 Fine Pitch Gold Bump
與高精度封裝能力的要求亦同步提高。

的 Electrical Path 越短越有利於降低寄生效應與訊號損耗，因此 Flip-Chip 及 Bump-based
interconnect 的重要性提升 ，Gold Bump 的應用亦由傳統 DDI、RF 逐步延伸至 TIA、PD、Driver
及 Modulator 等高速光通訊元件。

圖三. 金凸塊製程

資料來源: 國祥貿易、國泰證期研究部整理

隨光通訊由單通道 100G 升級至 200G，訊號傳輸頻率提升，使傳統打線封裝因導線較長而產
生更明顯的寄生電感 、 訊號損耗及雜訊干擾 ， 因此高速光通訊晶片逐步導入金凸塊(Gold Bump)，
藉由縮短晶片間的電性連接距離，改善訊號完整性。接收端 (Rx)方面，光偵測器(PD)將接收到
的光訊號轉換為微弱電訊號，再由跨阻放大器(TIA)放大，由於訊號強度極低，PD 與 TIA 之間
須透過金凸塊縮短傳輸路徑，降低雜訊及訊號失真；發射端(Tx)方面，Driver 接收來自 DSP 的
高速電訊號，並驅動調變器 (Modulator)將電訊號轉換為光訊號的調變資訊，因此 Driver 與
Modulator 同樣需要低寄生效應的高速電性互連，以維持訊號品質。隨 1.6T 及 3.2T 光收發模
組逐步導入，金凸塊將由接收端 TIA、PD 延伸至發射端 Driver、Modulator，帶動光通訊金凸
塊需求及相關封裝產值持續提升。

公司簡介
頎邦(6147.TT)成立於 1997 年，總部位於新竹科學園區，2002 年於櫃買中心掛牌，為台灣主
要半導體封裝測試廠之一，長期專注於顯示驅動 IC(Display Driver IC, DDI )後段製程。公司由
金凸塊(Gold Bumping)製程起家 ， 並逐步建立晶圓測試(Chip Probing, CP)、 晶圓研磨與切割、
COF(Chip on Film)、COG(Chip on Glass)、WLCSP 等完整封裝測試能力，是少數能提供 DDI
由凸塊、測試至後段封裝完整製程服務的廠商；公司官方將自身定位為全球最大顯示驅動IC 封
裝測試廠之一。頎邦目前於台灣設有新竹科學園區力行、展業、研發廠、新竹產業園區光復廠，
以及高雄南六、南一廠等生產據點，其中新竹主要負責 Bumping、Testing、Grinding/Dicing
及 Assembly，高雄則以測試、封裝及 COF T ape製造為主。

頎邦核心技術為晶圓級凸塊製程，公司透過薄膜、黃光及電鍍製程，在晶片 Pad 上形成 Gold
Bump，並進一步發展銅鎳金凸塊、RDL 等相關技術。金凸塊過去主要應用於 DDI，搭配 COF
或 COG 等 Flip-Chip 封裝，以滿足顯示驅動晶片高 I/O、Fine Pitch 及薄型化需求；目前公司
相關製程已可支援不同尺寸晶圓，且由傳統矽基晶圓延伸至 GaAs、GaN、SiC 及 LiT aO3等化
合物半導體材料。除封裝測試服務外，公司亦具備 Flexible Tape-and-Reel Circuit Substrate
及 Chip Tray 等產品，使其在 DDI 供應鏈涵蓋由凸塊、測試、封裝至部分材料與載具的垂直整
合能力。

產品應用方面，頎邦過去高度集中於 DDI，但近年持續利用既有 Gold Bump 及 Wafer Test能
力拓展非驅動 IC 業務。依 2026 年公司法說資訊，DDI 目前仍約占營收 60–65%，主要應用於
手機、TV 與 NB/PC；RF Front-end 約占 20%，RFID 約占 3%，其餘則包含電源管理、化合物
半導體及其他新產品。相較過去 DDI 占比逾九成，公司產品組合已逐步朝 RF、RFID 及高附加
價值封裝應用分散，降低成熟顯示驅動 IC 市場對營運的單一影響。

2026 年起，矽光子(Silicon Photonics )成為頎邦另一項重要新業務。隨 AI 資料中心光通訊由
100G/lane 升級至 200G/lane，PD、TIA、Driver 及 Modulator 等高速元件對短距離、高訊
號完整性的互連要求提高，部分架構由傳統 Wire Bond 轉向 Flip-Chip／Gold Bump，使頎邦
既有金凸塊技術開始由 DDI 延伸至高速光通訊。公司目前已切入TIA、Photodetector、Driver
及 Modulator 等元件 ， 其中部分產品已於2026 年量產 ， 並持續擴大相關客戶與專案 ； 截至2026
年第三季，DDI 仍占營收六成以上，但矽光業務已成為非 DDI 產品中成長最快的項目之一。

在全球布局方面，頎邦除台灣既有生產基地外，近年亦因應客戶供應鏈在地化與地緣政治需求
擴大海外布局。公司 2026 年於馬來西亞檳城啟用新廠，投資規模約 US$200mn，主要目的為
增加海外生產彈性 、 滿足客戶Non-China/Non-T aiwan供應鏈需求並降低單一地區製造風險；
公司亦於 2025 年永續報告中明確將馬來西亞據點擴建列為強化全球產能配置與供應鏈韌性的
核心措施之一。

頎邦 ESG 政策
頎邦(6147.TT)將永續發展納入公司治理及日常營運架構，ESG 政策主要涵蓋公司治理、環境永
續、員工與社會責任及供應鏈管理四大方向。公司依循《上市上櫃公司永續發展實務守則》及
責任商業聯盟行為準則(RBA Code of Conduct )等國內外規範訂定永續政策，核心原則包括健
全公司治理與資訊揭露、降低溫室氣體與資源消耗、保障勞動人權與職業安全，以及要求供應
鏈共同落實企業社會責任。治理架構方面，公司於董事會層級建立永續監督機制，並設有永續
發展指導委員會及永續發展執行委員會，下設公司治理、環境安全與供應鏈管理、員工權益關
懷、資訊安全及社會參與等功能小組，定期追蹤重大永續議題、溫室氣體盤查、IFRS S1/S2 導
入及各項年度 ESG 目標執行情形，再向董事會報告。

環境面以降低製造端碳排、能源效率提升及再生能源導入為主要政策方向。 頎邦依 TCFD 架構
辨識氣候轉型及實體風險，並以 ISO 14064-1 進行溫室氣體盤查，盤查範圍目前涵蓋台灣六個
營運據點 ， 自2021 年起並導入第三方查證 。2025 年 Scope 1 與 Scope 2 合計排放量為 150,934
公噸 CO₂e，YoY 下降 2.36%，較 2021 基準年下降 11.89%，其中 Scope 2 電力相關排放占整
體排放 74.85%，顯示外購電力仍為主要減碳重點。公司設定 2026 年 Scope 1+2 較 2021 年
減少 12%、2030 年減少 23%，長期則配合台灣 2050 淨零路徑。

能源管理方面，公司透過 ISO 50001 架構、設備汰換、機台操作優化及製程效率改善降低能源
強度。2025 年共執行 27 項重點節能方案，節電約 595 萬度、節電率 1.88%，約減少 2,820
公噸 CO₂e 排放；同期能源使用密集度 YoY 下降 3.8%。公司並持續增加太陽能與綠電使用，
2025 年再生能源實際使用量約 76.1 萬度 ，2030 年目標提高至 4,300 萬度 。 由於目前外購電力
仍占總能源使用約 99.4%，再生能源占比仍低，因此未來環境政策的主要執行重點將持續落在
能源效率改善與綠電導入速度。

水資源及循環經濟則與頎邦的 Bumping、Grinding/Dicing 及 T ape製程高度相關。 公司將製
程廢水依矽粉、酸鹼、有機物及重金屬等性質分流處理，回收水再投入製程或次級用途。2025
年總用水量為 3,328 ML， 因產量與製程需求增加而YoY 成長 8.59%， 其中製程回收水約1,332
ML；切割研磨製程水回收率為 78.6%，公司設定 2026 年提升至 82%、2030 年達 85%。在廢
棄物方面，管理原則依序為源頭減量、再利用及末端處理，2025 年廢溶劑回收率達 87.68%，
並推動矽污泥 、 含銅污泥 、 氫氟酸及Tray 塑膠邊料資源化 ， 其中再生塑料投入比例為23.48%；
後續目標包括廢塑膠回收率提高至 90%以上。

空污管理方面 ， 公司針對製程VOCs 及 PFCs 等排放進行設備改善 ， 其中2025 年力行廠沸石轉
輪 VOC 處理設備正式取得許可啟用，VOCs 排放量較 2022 基準年下降 42.16%，已超過原先
2030 年下降 40%的目標；此外，公司於電漿蝕刻製程加裝尾氣處理設備，2025 年 PFCs 排放
減少約 6,004 公噸 CO₂e。

社會面主要聚焦勞動人權、人才留任與職業安全。 頎邦人權政策參考《聯合國企業與人權指導
原則》 、ILO 相關原則、 《世界人權宣言》及RBA 規範，涵蓋禁止強迫勞動、青年勞工、工時、
薪酬福利、人道待遇、不歧視及自由結社等議題，並透過年度 RBA 自評、內部 ESG 稽核及法
規鑑別進行人權風險評估。2025 年人權與性別平權相關課程均有 10,112 人次參與，公司亦設
置員工申訴及溝通管道；年度員工滿意度由2024 年的 3.98 分提升至 2025 年的 4.08 分，惟問
卷參與率約 41.4%，未達原訂 50%目標，公司後續將以每年滿意度分數提升至少 2%作為改善
方向。

重要訊息 
我們近期拜訪管理層更新產業動態與公司近況。  
評論及分析  
3Q26 營收符合預期。 3Q26 營收 5.59 億元，年增 32.5%，大致符合市場共
識 5.64 億元。台灣電商環境成長維持溫和， 1H26 電商銷售額年增
11.3%，排除其他零售業的實體電商 D2C 銷售額年增 5.3%，7M-8M26 電
商銷售額分別年增 5.5/8.5% 。管理層看好中大型品牌因原有小型電商系統
無法支撐 OMO 擴張而轉換平台，91APP 以全通路 IMS（線上、門市、倉儲
庫存打通）、 Super APP 系統整合與在地團隊勝出，同時進行營收結構轉
型，GMV 抽成的系統使用費占比由 1H25 59.6% 降至 1H26 的 48.6%。 
iCHEF 整併快於預期。 iCHEF 團隊已於 7 月遷入總部，快於原訂年底之目
標，嚴格的營業費用與人力管理已讓 iCHEF 2Q26 營業利益率顯著提升，透
過 91APP 優勢與擅長系統整合之能力，iCHEF 已取得中大型連鎖餐飲集團簽
約採用，線上刷卡轉入 91APP Payments 以較低手續費擴大金流服務滲透，
管理層看好 1Q27 併表效應結束後仍可提供不俗的營收成長貢獻。  
AgentOne  2027 上線鎖定 Agentic AI 商機。 AgentOne 於 7 月客戶大會
發表， 2H26 與客戶進行  POC，2027 正式上線。首波主打為 MediaOne
（廣告企劃到投放的自動化）與  EngageOne （個人化行銷），也已接入  
iCHEF 餐飲場景。目標市場是  91APP 既有的 KA/SKA 品牌與通路客戶，優
勢在於客戶第一方數據都存放在  91APP 平台，可直接執行複雜工作流並完
善治理。AgentOne 變現路徑： (1)GMV 提升帶動系統使用費；(2) 訂閱與  
token 費；(3)客戶擴大廣告投放預算。為該司 2027 主要成長動能之一 。 
投資建議  
凱基正向看待 AgentOne 直擊企業轉型需求。目前股價交易在 2027 市場共
識每股盈餘 6.23 元之 8.7 倍 PE(約當 5 年平均之- 1.5 倍標準差)。 
投資風險  
D2C 成長不如預期，Agent 產品滲透率有限。

AgentOne 讓企業 AI 從對話走向執行
重要訊息
我們近期拜訪管理層更新產業動態與公司近況。
評論及分析
3Q26 營收符合預期。 3Q26 營收 5.59 億元，年增 32.5%，大致符合市場共
識 5.64 億元。台灣電商環境成長維持溫和， 1H26 電商銷售額年增
11.3%，排除其他零售業的實體電商 D2C 銷售額年增 5.3%，7M-8M26 電
商銷售額分別年增 5.5/8.5% 。管理層看好中大型品牌因原有小型電商系統
無法支撐 OMO 擴張而轉換平台，91APP 以全通路 IMS（線上、門市、倉儲
庫存打通）、 Super APP 系統整合與在地團隊勝出，同時進行營收結構轉
型，GMV 抽成的系統使用費占比由 1H25 59.6% 降至 1H26 的 48.6%。
iCHEF 整併快於預期。 iCHEF 團隊已於 7 月遷入總部，快於原訂年底之目
標，嚴格的營業費用與人力管理已讓 iCHEF 2Q26 營業利益率顯著提升，透
過 91APP 優勢與擅長系統整合之能力，iCHEF 已取得中大型連鎖餐飲集團簽
約採用，線上刷卡轉入 91APP Payments 以較低手續費擴大金流服務滲透，
管理層看好 1Q27 併表效應結束後仍可提供不俗的營收成長貢獻。
AgentOne  2027 上線鎖定 Agentic AI 商機。 AgentOne 於 7 月客戶大會
發表， 2H26 與客戶進行  POC，2027 正式上線。首波主打為 MediaOne
（廣告企劃到投放的自動化）與  EngageOne （個人化行銷），也已接入
iCHEF 餐飲場景。目標市場是  91APP 既有的 KA/SKA 品牌與通路客戶，優
勢在於客戶第一方數據都存放在  91APP 平台，可直接執行複雜工作流並完
善治理。AgentOne 變現路徑： (1)GMV 提升帶動系統使用費；(2) 訂閱與
token 費；(3)客戶擴大廣告投放預算。為該司 2027 主要成長動能之一 。
投資建議
凱基正向看待 AgentOne 直擊企業轉型需求。目前股價交易在 2027 市場共
識每股盈餘 6.23 元之 8.7 倍 PE(約當 5 年平均之- 1.5 倍標準差)。
投資風險
D2C 成長不如預期，Agent 產品滲透率有限。

  系統電營運主力將轉移至 BBU 相關應用： 系統電子工業股份有限公司成立於1977
年，原專注在車用電子、能源、通訊、電玩遊戲。近年公司陸續進行業務調整及轉
型 ， 將業務分為汽車電子 、 工業物聯網 、AI 資料中心能源系統管理三大事業 ，2015
年推出藍牙胎壓偵測器(BLE TPMS)， 目前主要經營業務內容為車用胎壓偵測系統 、
車用電子產品、綠色能源及儲能設備、電源供應器，並獲有多項專利，並持續擴大
BLE TPMS 應用在歐美 OE 前裝市場，如新能源訂動車、大客車車隊、皮卡等。近
期受到資料中心用電需求增加，系統電 BBU 相關產品將開始出貨。1H26 產品比
重：TPMS 46%、工業電腦 38%、AI 資料中心能源系統及其他 16%。 
3Q26 強固型工業電腦出貨旺，：系統電 9 月營收 3.67 億元(+12.04%MoM，
+17.87%YoY)，連續三個月創下歷史新高，主係因強固型電腦產品出貨。雖 BBU
及無人機相關產品尚未大量出貨，然在工業電腦領域，受惠產業趨勢帶動，如農耕
車及無人載具相關應用成長快速，使系統電 3Q26 營收 10.14 億元(+13%QoQ，
+24%YoY)，研究處預估毛利率 23.2%(+1ppt QoQ，+1.9ppt YoY)，因積極投入
研發及新產品設計使營業費用較高，稅後淨利 0.04 億元，稅後 EPS 為 0.02 元。 
4Q26 兩大專案 BBU 及無人機小量出貨 ：先前耕於已久的 BBU 產品將於十月開始
出貨 ， 初期以3kW 產品為主 ， 系統電已完成建置 2 條全自動 與 1 條半自動 BBU
產線。無人機方面，包含軍用及微型軍警偵察需求強勁，產線亦完成建置。研究處
預期 4Q26 營收 11.17 億元(+10.2%QoQ，+28%YoY)，毛利率 24%(+0.8ppt 
QoQ，-0.6ppt YoY)，稅後淨利 0.07 億元，稅後 EPS 為 0.03 元。預估 2026 年營
收 38.9 億元(+14.7%YoY)，毛利率 23.6%(+0.1pts YoY) ，稅後淨利 0.24 億元(-
54.3%YoY)，稅後 EPS 為 0.11 元。 
2027 年迎來營運收成期：展望 2027 年，以三大事業體區分，工業電腦方面將聚
焦於邊緣算力模組、GCS 地面控制站，部門產品毛利率最佳，有利於獲利表現；AI
資料中心能源系統方面，BBU 產品將開始大量出貨，並持續擴充產能，預估部門
營收將年增 328%，並將增加 3-4 條 BBU 產線，因應未來新產品的加入；TPMS
業務收到車市影響，營運相對平淡。綜上所述，系統電2027 年營運將開始收成過
去在無人載具及 BBU 電源產品的投入，研究處預期 2027 年營收 61.68 億元
(+58.5%YoY)，毛利率 24.9%(+1.3pts YoY) ，稅後淨利 5.41 億元，稅後 EPS 為
2.36 元。

  系統電營運主力將轉移至 BBU 相關應用： 系統電子工業股份有限公司成立於1977
年，原專注在車用電子、能源、通訊、電玩遊戲。近年公司陸續進行業務調整及轉
型 ， 將業務分為汽車電子 、 工業物聯網 、AI 資料中心能源系統管理三大事業 ，2015
年推出藍牙胎壓偵測器(BLE TPMS)， 目前主要經營業務內容為車用胎壓偵測系統 、
車用電子產品、綠色能源及儲能設備、電源供應器，並獲有多項專利，並持續擴大
BLE TPMS 應用在歐美 OE 前裝市場，如新能源訂動車、大客車車隊、皮卡等。近
期受到資料中心用電需求增加，系統電 BBU 相關產品將開始出貨。1H26 產品比
重：TPMS 46%、工業電腦 38%、AI 資料中心能源系統及其他 16%。
3Q26 強固型工業電腦出貨旺，：系統電 9 月營收 3.67 億元(+12.04%MoM，
+17.87%YoY)，連續三個月創下歷史新高，主係因強固型電腦產品出貨。雖 BBU
及無人機相關產品尚未大量出貨，然在工業電腦領域，受惠產業趨勢帶動，如農耕
車及無人載具相關應用成長快速，使系統電 3Q26 營收 10.14 億元(+13%QoQ，
+24%YoY)，研究處預估毛利率 23.2%(+1ppt QoQ，+1.9ppt YoY)，因積極投入
研發及新產品設計使營業費用較高，稅後淨利 0.04 億元，稅後 EPS 為 0.02 元。
4Q26 兩大專案 BBU 及無人機小量出貨 ：先前耕於已久的 BBU 產品將於十月開始
出貨 ， 初期以3kW 產品為主 ， 系統電已完成建置 2 條全自動 與 1 條半自動 BBU
產線。無人機方面，包含軍用及微型軍警偵察需求強勁，產線亦完成建置。研究處
預期 4Q26 營收 11.17 億元(+10.2%QoQ，+28%YoY)，毛利率 24%(+0.8ppt
QoQ，-0.6ppt YoY)，稅後淨利 0.07 億元，稅後 EPS 為 0.03 元。預估 2026 年營
收 38.9 億元(+14.7%YoY)，毛利率 23.6%(+0.1pts YoY) ，稅後淨利 0.24 億元(-
54.3%YoY)，稅後 EPS 為 0.11 元。
2027 年迎來營運收成期：展望 2027 年，以三大事業體區分，工業電腦方面將聚
焦於邊緣算力模組、GCS 地面控制站，部門產品毛利率最佳，有利於獲利表現；AI
資料中心能源系統方面，BBU 產品將開始大量出貨，並持續擴充產能，預估部門
營收將年增 328%，並將增加 3-4 條 BBU 產線，因應未來新產品的加入；TPMS
業務收到車市影響，營運相對平淡。綜上所述，系統電2027 年營運將開始收成過
去在無人載具及 BBU 電源產品的投入，研究處預期 2027 年營收 61.68 億元
(+58.5%YoY)，毛利率 24.9%(+1.3pts YoY) ，稅後淨利 5.41 億元，稅後 EPS 為
2.36 元。

testing and the emerging CPO testing market. Leveraging its long-standing relationship 
with TSMC, HTSI has established capabilities across electrical test engineering, 
customised test equipment, thermal control modules, probe cards, and CPO testing 
solutions. We forecast revenue growth of 127%/152%/78% in 2026E/27E/28E, driven 
by increasing adoption of thermal control modules for wafer-level test and initial 
deployment of CPO insertion 2 and insertion 3 test equipment through ficonTEC. 
Additional 2028E growth drivers include reflow tools, laser clean solutions, and MEMS 
probe cards. The stock trades at 27/15x 2027/28E PE, versus ~35x NTM PE for handler-
equipment peers, offering re-rating potential as sales scale, new products are qualified, 
and its CPO presence expands. See our companion testing deep dive sector note.
Shift-left beneficiary with exceptional thermal control modules
Thermal control modules should be HTSI's largest growth driver over the next several 
years. We expect increasing chip power consumption, rising package complexity, and 
tighter probe pitches to drive adoption of advanced thermal control solutions used 
alongside leading-edge probers, in additional to more wafer level insertions and longer 
test time. We estimate HTSI will ship approximately 3,000 thermal-control modules in 
2027E, up from around 1,200 units in 2026E, sales contribution rise from ~30% in 
Q226 to >50% of sales by 2027E. The launch of its second-generation platform in 
2027E, which carries 25-50% higher ASPs, should further improve profitability. We 
forecast GM expansion from 55.5% in 2026E to 58.3%/60.0% in 2027E/28E.
Unique position to capture CPO upside
Through its partnership with German optical-automation leader ficonTEC, HTSI is 
positioned to participate in the initial ramp of CPO testing equipment. HTSI supports 
local manufacturing, installation, automation and after-sales service, making it a key 
enabler of volume production. We estimate HTSI captures approximately 30% of 
equipment value across the 40 insertion 2 and 70 insertion 3 systems we forecast for 
delivery in 2027E, with further potential upside in 2028E as adoption expands.

Q: Will insertion 2 of CPO testing process be skipped?
No. We believe concerns surrounding insertion 2 adoption are overdone. While some industry 
participants favor bypassing insertion 2 due to throughput and ROI considerations, doing so increases 
the risk of defective optical engines being identified only after the components are delivered to 
OSATs, creating yield accountability challenges and higher packaging losses. Based on our industry 
studies, we expect insertion 2 testing to remain an important part of the CPO workflow over at least 
the next two years as the industry focuses on improving PIC yields and overall testing efficiency.

The economics of advanced packaging reinforce this trend. Heterogeneous integration, 
chiplet architectures and 2.5D/3D packaging significantly increase package value, while 
defects identified late in the manufacturing process can lead to substantial scrap costs. 
To mitigate this risk, foundries and OSATs such as TSMC and ASE employ distributed 
testing flows incorporating KGD, known-good-stack (KGS) and assembly test screening, 
to catch defects before the components enter a multi-week packaging cycle (>2 weeks 
for CoW and 2 weeks for oS). The importance of these tests rises as AI clusters become 
increasingly dependent on component reliability and low defective-parts-per-million 
(DPPM) rates. Given the multiplicative yield degradation, a 300bps yield decline at just 
one manufacturing stage (e.g. dropping from 99.5% to 96.5%) reduces overall 
integrated four-stage yield from 98.0% to 95.0%; on a 500,000 unit ramp at US
$10,000 per unit, this 3% scrap delta translates into around US$150m in unrecoverable 
losses given >6-month manufacturing lead times.
At the same time, rising chip power consumption is increasing the technical difficulty of 
wafer-level testing. As chip thermal design power scales beyond 1,000W and power 
density is expected by the industry to surge another 8x by 2030, traditional wafer-level 
chip probe (WLCP) encounters severe physical bottlenecks. Finer probe pitches and 
higher power densities increase the risk of overheating, probe needle burnout and yield 
degradation, creating demand for more advanced probing and thermal-control 
solutions.

CPO testing fuelling future growth for semiconductor testing
As interconnect bottlenecks increasingly shift from the memory wall to the copper wall, 
we believe co-packaged optics (CPO) adoption is inevitable over the longer term. Testing 
remains one of the key bottlenecks to CPO deployment, as optical validation differs 
fundamentally from the electrical testing processes that have dominated semiconductor 
manufacturing for decades. As a result, CPO is creating a new testing opportunity across 
the semiconductor equipment and consumables ecosystem. We have written 
extensively on CPO and opportunities that it brings to the semiconductor supply chain, 
see our CPO deep dive , our thoughts on CPO timing, 2026 SiPhIA conference 
takeaways, and SEMICON 2026 takeaways.
Various test equipment suppliers are scrambling to come up with ideal testing 
equipment across the four insertions of CPO testing, with solutions to ensure both 
optical and electrical signal integrity of the CPO solutions. The four insertions are:
 Insertion 1: Electronic IC (EIC)/Photonic IC (PIC) test. Single-side wafer test 
that has dedicated probe cards to test the fabricated EIC/PIC wafers.
 Insertion 2: Optical/Electrical test. Double sided wafer test, testing the hybrid 
bonded (e.g. via TSMC's COUPE) EIC and PIC wafers by an opto-electrical test that 
verifies the electrical signals on the top and optical signal on the bottom of the 
hybrid bonded wafers.
 Insertion 3: Optical engine (OE) test. The OE tests are done to ensure the 
quality of the OEs and with FAU (Fiber Array Unit) attached, to ensure the signal 
integrity of the OEs. The testing equipment needs to be able to handle 224G per 
channel data rates, requiring high unit per hour (UPH) throughput, meticulous dirt 
mitigation, and maintaining a near 100% contact rating on high-speed sockets.
 Insertion 4: ASIC final test. This final test step is established post the OEs are 
packaged together with the ASIC. The complete ASIC package (now with CPO) is 
now tested for opto-electrical functionalities.
As it stands, insertion 2 and insertion 3 are the two areas where there are the most 
debates in the industry. Insertion 3 suppliers such as Chroma has noted the trend of 
“shift-to-middle” paradigm centered on insertion 3. In high-density scale-out switches 
deploying up to 32 optical engines (e.g. Nvidia’s Spectrum-X architectures), any OE 
defect results in package scrap at the CoWoS level, making 100% known good die 
(KGD) validation at the singulated OE stage an absolute commercial requirement.

segment, as CPO are not direct HTSI products, but rather sales recognition via its 
partnership with ficonTEC.
 Probe card design, manufacturing, and cleaning materials: HTSI delivers a 
comprehensive product portfolio that supports the entire probe card life-cycle. For 
probe cards, they supply membrane, cantilever, and vertical probe cards. As they 
are small in scale, HTSI targets niche probe card applications such as RF, 5G/6G, 
millimeter wave, LCD driver, low end logics, TIA (Transimpedance Amplifier), etc. In 
addition to the three existing probe technologies, HTSI also collaborates with MJC 
in Japan for MEMS probe development, targeting sales in 2028E for high-end, AI/
HPC related applications. Cleaning materials is another important business within 
this segment, as HTSI source and process sand paper or other materials to offer 
cleaning sheets to clean the probe cards, removing oxidations, unwanted particles 
and substances that accumulated on the probe cards during the testing process.
The sales resiliency in the coming years mainly stems from its robust relationship with key 
industry players, especially as an engineering and service provider with TSMC for testing 
solutions. This sets up a solid foundation for its customized equipment business, as they 
know the specific testing bottleneck to tackle. For instance, as Hermes-Epitek 
manufacturers the probers for Tokyo Electron (TEL) and HTSI helps with installation, 
services, and maintenance of the probers, they understand the thermal bottlenecks that 
the wafer-level test industry has been facing and can effectively come up with module 
solutions to solve this.
Margins set to expand with value-added products and services
The company has demonstrated strong execution in advanced wafer-level testing, with 
H126 revenue of NT$2.2bn already exceeding 90% of FY25 revenue (NT$2.4bn). 
Profitability has also improved significantly, with GM increasing from 42.1% in 2025 to 
54.9% in H126.
With share of value-added products and services set to rise in 2027E in sales mix, HTSI is 
set to see GM and operating leverage expansion. As a niche engineering service provider 
that has robust ties to leading foundries and OSATs, we believe HTSI has substantial 
pricing power and estimate HTSI' GM for thermal control modules to be around 65%, 
with GM for CPO equipment of around 60% as HTSI provides an engineering-service-
like business for it. We believe these factors will help the company to reach a 60% long-
term GM range.
OPM is also set to expand with customized equipment sales rise in total sales mix. If we 
exclude the one-time expense to be recognized during Q326 for employee stock 
benefits (we estimate around NT$1bn), YoY opex growth will be around 99% for 
2027E, with downside risk if the company conducts tight cost control measures. We 
forecast the company's OPM will expand from 19.5% in 2026E, to 44.3%/47.0% in 
2027/28E.

Despite a 264% YTD share-price increase, HTSI still trades at just 15x 2028E P/E. We 
believe market expectations for 2027E CPO testing equipment shipments remain 
conservative, particularly for insertion 2 equipment. Based on our industry analysis, we 
estimate HTSI will deliver 40 insertion 2 and 70 insertion 3 systems in 2027E, this should 
be higher than the market's expectation of no insertion 2 and limited insertion 3 
shipment due to engineering bottleneck. We also see further upside in 2028E as CPO 
adoption expands. Our reverse DCF analysis indicates that the current market price 
implies only a 17% long-term sales CAGR vs our estimate of 27% and long-term GM 
level of 33% vs our estimate of 61%. We see scope for re-rating.
We believe the market is not fully reflecting three key growth drivers:
1) Shift-left testing is still underappreciated.
As advanced packaging costs rise and AI accelerators become increasingly complex, 
more thorough testing is done at the wafer-level. This should drive sustained demand 
for HTSI's thermal control modules, probe card consumables, and other wafer-level 
testing solutions.
2) CPO revenue potential remains underestimated.
Investor expectations for 2027 CPO equipment shipments, particularly insertion 2 
testing systems, remain conservative. Based on our industry studies, we forecast HTSI 
will deliver 40 insertion 2 and 70 insertion 3 systems in 2027E, with further potential 
upside in 2028E as CPO adoption broadens.
3) New products provide additional optionality.
Beyond its core businesses, HTSI is expanding into higher-value solutions including mass-
reflow tools, MEMS probe cards and laser cleaning systems, creating incremental 
growth opportunities that we believe are largely absent from current expectations.
We value HTSI using 31x average 2028E PE, underpinned by a 32% 2027-31E earnings 
CAGR. We use 2028E PE as our view is that 2028 is the year for thermal control modules 
and CPO adoption grow from the initial ramping up stage to mass adoption stage. We 
believe using handlers as a peer group is justifiable for a unique company like HTSI, with 
thermal control modules for chip probing sharing similar characteristics as active thermal 
control used for final test, in addition to Hon Precision and Chroma having exposure to 
CPO test equipment. For equipment vendors, the peer group's average NTM PE post 
2022 is around 35x, and the group is currently trading at around 41x NTM PE (see 
What's Priced In chart).

Company Description
Hermes Testing Solutions (HTSI) was founded in 2004 in Hsinchu, 
Taiwan. It focuses on providing semiconductor testing and 
inspecting solutions, equipment installation, technical support, 
and maintenance services. Its main business segments are 
customized semiconductor equipment, engineering services, and 
probe cards and other materials.
Industry Outlook
New iterations of semiconductors, especially for AI / HPC 
applications, are set to increase in both front-end wafer 
fabrication advancements and back-end packaging complexities 
with each iterations. With the industry now moves to utilize 
"shift left", chip probing and its relevant supply chain will be key 
beneficiaries of this trend which we believe will unlock multi-
year, secular growth trends.

Hermes Testing Solutions (HTSI) was founded in 2004 in Hsinchu, Taiwan. It focuses on 
providing semiconductor testing and inspecting solutions, equipment installation, technical 
support, and maintenance services. Its main business segments are customized 
semiconductor equipment, engineering services, and probe cards and other materials.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We value Hermes Testing based on PE methodology.
Risks for the semis industry:
- Geopolitical uncertainties: Geopolitical uncertainties including tariffs and more export 
control could negatively impact semis cycle, and a downturn would lead to slower demand in 
the overall market and moderating capacity expansion.
- Meaningful deceleration of new technology development: Slower demand and less 
investment are expected If there is meaningful deceleration of new technology development 
such as Cloud AI, autonomous driving, etc.
- Rising utility cost: Larger-than-expected utility cost increases would further pressure 
profitability. Rising utility costs in Taiwan have negatively impacted margins for Taiwan tech 
companies.
Company risks:
- Faster- or slower-than-expected front-end/CoWoS capacity expansion: This could result in 
Hermes Testing gaining/losing equipment orders from major foundries and OSATs.
- Competitors achieving technological advancement: Potential risk of competition (from 
either local or foreign companies) achieving technological advancements could result in 
Hermes Testing losing market share from major foundries and OSATs.
- Better- or worse-than-expected AI growth: Better- or worse-than-expected AI growth could 
lead to a ramp-up or a slowdown of equipment orders from major foundries and OSATs to 
Hermes Testing, affecting long-term revenue growth potential.
- Slowdown or delay of new technological advancement: A potential slowdown or delay of 
the rollout for technological advancements for technologies such as SoIC, CoPoS, and CPO, 
would limit future equipment orders.
- Increase of raw material costs: Rising raw material costs may directly impact Hermes 
Testing’s margins for equipment shipments.

ab 8 October 2026
Global Research
Initiation of Coverage
Hermes Testing Solutions
Shifting-left, scaling-up: dual catalysts in chip
probing and CPO
Jack-of-all-trades for bespoke testing solutions in the semiconductor industry
We initiate coverage of Hermes Testing (HTSI) with a Buy rating and NT$8,880 PT. HTSI is
uniquely positioned to benefit from two key semiconductor testing trends: shift-left
testing and the emerging CPO testing market. Leveraging its long-standing relationship
with TSMC, HTSI has established capabilities across electrical test engineering,
customised test equipment, thermal control modules, probe cards, and CPO testing
solutions. We forecast revenue growth of 127%/152%/78% in 2026E/27E/28E, driven
by increasing adoption of thermal control modules for wafer-level test and initial
deployment of CPO insertion 2 and insertion 3 test equipment through ficonTEC.
Additional 2028E growth drivers include reflow tools, laser clean solutions, and MEMS
probe cards. The stock trades at 27/15x 2027/28E PE, versus ~35x NTM PE for handler-
equipment peers, offering re-rating potential as sales scale, new products are qualified,
and its CPO presence expands. See our companion testing deep dive sector note.
Shift-left beneficiary with exceptional thermal control modules
Thermal control modules should be HTSI's largest growth driver over the next several
years. We expect increasing chip power consumption, rising package complexity, and
tighter probe pitches to drive adoption of advanced thermal control solutions used
alongside leading-edge probers, in additional to more wafer level insertions and longer
test time. We estimate HTSI will ship approximately 3,000 thermal-control modules in
2027E, up from around 1,200 units in 2026E, sales contribution rise from ~30% in
Q226 to >50% of sales by 2027E. The launch of its second-generation platform in
2027E, which carries 25-50% higher ASPs, should further improve profitability. We
forecast GM expansion from 55.5% in 2026E to 58.3%/60.0% in 2027E/28E.
Unique position to capture CPO upside
Through its partnership with German optical-automation leader ficonTEC, HTSI is
positioned to participate in the initial ramp of CPO testing equipment. HTSI supports
local manufacturing, installation, automation and after-sales service, making it a key
enabler of volume production. We estimate HTSI captures approximately 30% of
equipment value across the 40 insertion 2 and 70 insertion 3 systems we forecast for
delivery in 2027E, with further potential upside in 2028E as adoption expands.
Valuation: initiate coverage with a Buy rating and price target NT$8,880
We forecast EPS of NT$29.1 in 2026E (including a one-off employee share purchase
programme impact), rising to NT$153.3/286.5 in 2027E/28E. Our NT$8,880 price target
is based on 31x average 2028E PE, versus handler-equipment peers forward PE at
roughly 35x, reflecting HTSI's unique exposure to both shift-left testing, CPO, and our
estimate of 32% LT earnings CAGR. We initiate with a Buy rating.

Q: Will HTSI be able to keep its moat within chip probing thermal control modules?
Yes. We expect HTSI's competitive position to strengthen as chip power consumption, package
complexity, and probe density continue to increase. The company is developing next-generation
thermal control solutions, including liquid cooling technologies, while also expanding into specialized
chuck solutions designed to address wafer warpage. In addition, HTSI's close collaboration with
TSMC, TEL, Advantest, and other OSATs should reinforce its position within advanced wafer-level
testing.
Q: Will insertion 2 of CPO testing process be skipped?
No. We believe concerns surrounding insertion 2 adoption are overdone. While some industry
participants favor bypassing insertion 2 due to throughput and ROI considerations, doing so increases
the risk of defective optical engines being identified only after the components are delivered to
OSATs, creating yield accountability challenges and higher packaging losses. Based on our industry
studies, we expect insertion 2 testing to remain an important part of the CPO workflow over at least
the next two years as the industry focuses on improving PIC yields and overall testing efficiency.
We initiate coverage of Hermes Testing (HTSI) with a Buy rating and NT$8,880 price target. HTSI
offers unique exposure to two of the semiconductor testing industry's most attractive growth drivers:
1) shift-left testing and 2) CPO testing. The industry's shift-left testing strategy will have more test
insertions move to the wafer level before packaging, in addition to longer CP time. Leveraging its
longstanding relationship with TSMC, HTSI has established capabilities across thermal control
modules, electrical-test engineering services, customized equipment, and emerging CPO testing
solutions. We believe there could be re-rating potential as sales scale, new products are qualified, and
its CPO presence expands.
TSMC and OSATs have been expanding their CoWoS capacities aggressively, from 40kwpm in 2024
to around 90 kwpm in 2025, and is tracking to expand CoWoS capacity toward 160kwpm in 2026E.
TSMC also ramped up expanding N3/N2 capacity, with multiple product launches from customers'
pipelines—Nvidia's Rubin, AMD's MI400 series/Venice CPU and other cloud ASICs—translating into
foreseeable, strong testing demand.
Despite a 264% YTD share-price increase, HTSI currently trades at just 15x of our 2028E EPS versus
handler-equipment peers forward PE at roughly 35x. We believe market expectations for 2027 CPO
testing equipment shipments remain conservative, particularly for insertion 2 equipment. Based on
our industry analysis, we estimate HTSI will deliver 40 insertion 2 and 70 insertion 3 systems in 2027E,
this should be higher than the market's expectation of no insertion 2 and limited insertion 3 shipment
due to engineering bottleneck. We also see further upside in 2028E as CPO adoption expands. Our
reverse DCF analysis indicates that the current market price implies only a 17% long-term sales CAGR
vs our estimate of 27% and long-term GM level of 33% vs our estimate of 61%. We see scope for
re-rating.

Testing TAM expanding with IC complexity: leaders likely to
outperform industry growth
Our central view is that testing content per AI accelerator is growing faster than
semiconductor unit volumes, creating a multi-year expansion in testing TAM. We believe
semiconductor testing is entering a period of structural growth as AI-driven chip
complexity increases testing intensity across wafer, package and system levels. The
industry's shift-left strategy, which moves more testing upstream in the semiconductor
manufacturing process, is resulting in longer and more frequent test insertions. As cloud
AI GPUs and ASICs become increasingly complex, additional testing is required to ensure
functionality, performance and yield, while reducing defective parts per million (DPPM).
More robust testing should improve deployment efficiency and lower the cost of
operating AI infrastructure.
Semiconductor testing generally comprises four stages: wafer/chip probing (CP), final
test (FT), system-level test (SLT), and burn-in. CP is conducted at the wafer-level before

Robust growth drivers across semiconductor testing
We believe HTSI is set to benefit from several semiconductor testing growth drivers and
capture the AI induced, expanding testing TAM. We see HTSI is uniquely positioned as
the main beneficiary of two of the strongest growth drivers within semiconductor
testing: testing shift-left and CPO.
Shift-left igniting secular growth for chip probing
Hermes Testing Solutions8 October 2026 ab 5
The industry's adoption of shift-left testing should drive a multi-year structural growth
opportunity for chip probing (CP) and its supply chain. As advanced packaging costs rise
and AI accelerators become increasingly complex, semiconductor manufacturers are
placing greater emphasis on identifying known-good dies (KGD) before packaging.

The economics of advanced packaging reinforce this trend. Heterogeneous integration,
chiplet architectures and 2.5D/3D packaging significantly increase package value, while
defects identified late in the manufacturing process can lead to substantial scrap costs.
To mitigate this risk, foundries and OSATs such as TSMC and ASE employ distributed
testing flows incorporating KGD, known-good-stack (KGS) and assembly test screening,
to catch defects before the components enter a multi-week packaging cycle (>2 weeks
for CoW and 2 weeks for oS). The importance of these tests rises as AI clusters become
increasingly dependent on component reliability and low defective-parts-per-million
(DPPM) rates. Given the multiplicative yield degradation, a 300bps yield decline at just
one manufacturing stage (e.g. dropping from 99.5% to 96.5%) reduces overall
integrated four-stage yield from 98.0% to 95.0%; on a 500,000 unit ramp at US
$10,000 per unit, this 3% scrap delta translates into around US$150m in unrecoverable
losses given >6-month manufacturing lead times.
At the same time, rising chip power consumption is increasing the technical difficulty of
wafer-level testing. As chip thermal design power scales beyond 1,000W and power
density is expected by the industry to surge another 8x by 2030, traditional wafer-level
chip probe (WLCP) encounters severe physical bottlenecks. Finer probe pitches and
higher power densities increase the risk of overheating, probe needle burnout and yield
degradation, creating demand for more advanced probing and thermal-control

CPO testing fuelling future growth for semiconductor testing
As interconnect bottlenecks increasingly shift from the memory wall to the copper wall,
we believe co-packaged optics (CPO) adoption is inevitable over the longer term. Testing
remains one of the key bottlenecks to CPO deployment, as optical validation differs
fundamentally from the electrical testing processes that have dominated semiconductor
manufacturing for decades. As a result, CPO is creating a new testing opportunity across
the semiconductor equipment and consumables ecosystem. We have written
extensively on CPO and opportunities that it brings to the semiconductor supply chain,
see our CPO deep dive , our thoughts on CPO timing, 2026 SiPhIA conference
takeaways, and SEMICON 2026 takeaways.
Various test equipment suppliers are scrambling to come up with ideal testing
equipment across the four insertions of CPO testing, with solutions to ensure both
optical and electrical signal integrity of the CPO solutions. The four insertions are:
 Insertion 1: Electronic IC (EIC)/Photonic IC (PIC) test. Single-side wafer test
that has dedicated probe cards to test the fabricated EIC/PIC wafers.
 Insertion 2: Optical/Electrical test. Double sided wafer test, testing the hybrid
bonded (e.g. via TSMC's COUPE) EIC and PIC wafers by an opto-electrical test that
verifies the electrical signals on the top and optical signal on the bottom of the
hybrid bonded wafers.
 Insertion 3: Optical engine (OE) test. The OE tests are done to ensure the
quality of the OEs and with FAU (Fiber Array Unit) attached, to ensure the signal
integrity of the OEs. The testing equipment needs to be able to handle 224G per
channel data rates, requiring high unit per hour (UPH) throughput, meticulous dirt
mitigation, and maintaining a near 100% contact rating on high-speed sockets.
 Insertion 4: ASIC final test. This final test step is established post the OEs are
packaged together with the ASIC. The complete ASIC package (now with CPO) is
now tested for opto-electrical functionalities.
As it stands, insertion 2 and insertion 3 are the two areas where there are the most
debates in the industry. Insertion 3 suppliers such as Chroma has noted the trend of
“shift-to-middle” paradigm centered on insertion 3. In high-density scale-out switches
deploying up to 32 optical engines (e.g. Nvidia’s Spectrum-X architectures), any OE
defect results in package scrap at the CoWoS level, making 100% known good die
(KGD) validation at the singulated OE stage an absolute commercial requirement.

Hermes Testing Solutions (HTSI) was founded in 2004 in Hsinchu, Taiwan, as a spin-off
from Hermes-Epitek. The company provides semiconductor testing and inspection
solutions, engineering services, customized equipment, and test consumables. HTSI
maintains a global service footprint across Taiwan (Hsinchu, Tainan), Mainland China
(Suzhou), Japan (Tokyo, Kumamoto), Singapore, Malaysia, and the United States
(Arizona), enabling close support for leading semiconductor customers.
Its main business segments are structured around three pillars:
 Semiconductor equipment and customized products: HTSI utilises a dual-
track strategy of independent R&D and also equipment agency sales. They offers

highly customized solutions designed to address specific client pain points and
bottlenecks. Key products include: thermal control modules that pair with a 1:1
ratio with wafer-level test probers, electron beam inspection equipment, white
light interference optical inspection systems, laser probe cleaning machines, and
the SYMPHONY fluxless reflow system.
 Testing equipment engineering services: The company operates the largest
engineering service team in Taiwan, consisting of over 340 technical professionals.
The engineering service team provides extensive equipment life-cycle support,
including installation, relocations, modification, testing, routine maintenance, and
repair services. CPO related equipment sales/services will be recognized within this
segment, as CPO are not direct HTSI products, but rather sales recognition via its
partnership with ficonTEC.
 Probe card design, manufacturing, and cleaning materials: HTSI delivers a
comprehensive product portfolio that supports the entire probe card life-cycle. For
probe cards, they supply membrane, cantilever, and vertical probe cards. As they
are small in scale, HTSI targets niche probe card applications such as RF, 5G/6G,
millimeter wave, LCD driver, low end logics, TIA (Transimpedance Amplifier), etc. In
addition to the three existing probe technologies, HTSI also collaborates with MJC
in Japan for MEMS probe development, targeting sales in 2028E for high-end, AI/
HPC related applications. Cleaning materials is another important business within
this segment, as HTSI source and process sand paper or other materials to offer
cleaning sheets to clean the probe cards, removing oxidations, unwanted particles
and substances that accumulated on the probe cards during the testing process.
The sales resiliency in the coming years mainly stems from its robust relationship with key
industry players, especially as an engineering and service provider with TSMC for testing
solutions. This sets up a solid foundation for its customized equipment business, as they
know the specific testing bottleneck to tackle. For instance, as Hermes-Epitek
manufacturers the probers for Tokyo Electron (TEL) and HTSI helps with installation,
services, and maintenance of the probers, they understand the thermal bottlenecks that
the wafer-level test industry has been facing and can effectively come up with module
solutions to solve this.

Despite a 264% YTD share-price increase, HTSI still trades at just 15x 2028E P/E. We
believe market expectations for 2027E CPO testing equipment shipments remain
conservative, particularly for insertion 2 equipment. Based on our industry analysis, we
estimate HTSI will deliver 40 insertion 2 and 70 insertion 3 systems in 2027E, this should
be higher than the market's expectation of no insertion 2 and limited insertion 3
shipment due to engineering bottleneck. We also see further upside in 2028E as CPO
adoption expands. Our reverse DCF analysis indicates that the current market price
implies only a 17% long-term sales CAGR vs our estimate of 27% and long-term GM
level of 33% vs our estimate of 61%. We see scope for re-rating.
We believe the market is not fully reflecting three key growth drivers:
1) Shift-left testing is still underappreciated.
As advanced packaging costs rise and AI accelerators become increasingly complex,
more thorough testing is done at the wafer-level. This should drive sustained demand
for HTSI's thermal control modules, probe card consumables, and other wafer-level
testing solutions.
2) CPO revenue potential remains underestimated.
Investor expectations for 2027 CPO equipment shipments, particularly insertion 2
testing systems, remain conservative. Based on our industry studies, we forecast HTSI
will deliver 40 insertion 2 and 70 insertion 3 systems in 2027E, with further potential
upside in 2028E as CPO adoption broadens.
3) New products provide additional optionality.
Beyond its core businesses, HTSI is expanding into higher-value solutions including mass-
reflow tools, MEMS probe cards and laser cleaning systems, creating incremental
growth opportunities that we believe are largely absent from current expectations.
We value HTSI using 31x average 2028E PE, underpinned by a 32% 2027-31E earnings
CAGR. We use 2028E PE as our view is that 2028 is the year for thermal control modules
and CPO adoption grow from the initial ramping up stage to mass adoption stage. We
believe using handlers as a peer group is justifiable for a unique company like HTSI, with
thermal control modules for chip probing sharing similar characteristics as active thermal
control used for final test, in addition to Hon Precision and Chroma having exposure to
CPO test equipment. For equipment vendors, the peer group's average NTM PE post
2022 is around 35x, and the group is currently trading at around 41x NTM PE (see
What's Priced In chart).

Company Description
Hermes Testing Solutions (HTSI) was founded in 2004 in Hsinchu, Taiwan. It focuses on
providing semiconductor testing and inspecting solutions, equipment installation, technical
support, and maintenance services. Its main business segments are customized
semiconductor equipment, engineering services, and probe cards and other materials.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We value Hermes Testing based on PE methodology.
Risks for the semis industry:
- Geopolitical uncertainties: Geopolitical uncertainties including tariffs and more export
control could negatively impact semis cycle, and a downturn would lead to slower demand in
the overall market and moderating capacity expansion.
- Meaningful deceleration of new technology development: Slower demand and less
investment are expected If there is meaningful deceleration of new technology development
such as Cloud AI, autonomous driving, etc.
- Rising utility cost: Larger-than-expected utility cost increases would further pressure
profitability. Rising utility costs in Taiwan have negatively impacted margins for Taiwan tech
companies.
Company risks:
- Faster- or slower-than-expected front-end/CoWoS capacity expansion: This could result in
Hermes Testing gaining/losing equipment orders from major foundries and OSATs.
- Competitors achieving technological advancement: Potential risk of competition (from
either local or foreign companies) achieving technological advancements could result in
Hermes Testing losing market share from major foundries and OSATs.
- Better- or worse-than-expected AI growth: Better- or worse-than-expected AI growth could
lead to a ramp-up or a slowdown of equipment orders from major foundries and OSATs to
Hermes Testing, affecting long-term revenue growth potential.
- Slowdown or delay of new technological advancement: A potential slowdown or delay of
the rollout for technological advancements for technologies such as SoIC, CoPoS, and CPO,
would limit future equipment orders.
- Increase of raw material costs: Rising raw material costs may directly impact Hermes
Testing’s margins for equipment shipments.

Largan Precision (3008.TW)
Better FAU visibility despite smartphone shortfall
CITI'S TAKE 
Largan’s 3Q26 earning was below expectation. 3Q26 revenue of 
NT$15.65bn (up 15% QoQ but down 11% YoY). GM declined to 42.2% with 
EPS reaching NT$39.6. Management attributed margin pressure to 
manufacturing yield challenges associated with increasingly complicated 
smartphone lenses, alongside the rising cost of renewable electricity. The 
latter is becoming a structural cost burden because of contractual 
commitments to customers. While yields are gradually improving, 
management see weakening smartphone order flow into 4Q26. 
Nevertheless, the management’s view on FAU development is positive 
and seeing great feedback and strong business engagement into the next 
generation CPO design. We reiterate our Buy and see any pull back on weak 
smartphone business as a great buying opportunity. 
CPO Strategy — Moving to integrated FAU and carrier assembly — The most 
important development during the call is Largan’s expanded product scope. 
Previously, the company primarily targeted Fiber Array alignment, positioning itself 
as a high-precision component supplier to established FAU manufacturers. 
Management now plans to produce FAU, purchase PMLA and other optical 
components, and perform precision optical coupling and assembly to deliver 
complete FAUs. It also intends to pursue the additional assembly step of mounting 
the FAU onto a carrier, which subsequently interfaces with the receptacle. This 
represents a meaningful expansion in value capture, moving Largan to higher-value 
integrated optical interconnect assemblies.
Customer qualification has progressed well, production starting in mid-2027 — 
Largan indicated that FA qualification is complete, and the automated pilot line is 
already operational and has been inspected repeatedly by the customer. Largan 
currently has one customer progressing toward commercial volume production, 
while several other customers, including CSP-related opportunities, are involved in 
next-generation development targeting 2028. Management expects the first scaled 
production lines to be ready around mid-2027, with meaningful FAU mass 
production potentially beginning in 2H27. Management also confirmed that recently 
acquired land and facilities have designated expansion purposes, primarily 
cleanrooms and production lines for FA/FAU rather than smartphone lenses.

Seeing multiple generation and years opportunities — Compared with these 
broader solutions providers, Largan remains primarily as a high-precision 
manufacturing and assembly specialist. Management described its current 
business relationship as closer to contract manufacturing, with direct discussions 
with end customers focused mainly on next-generation products. On product 
architecture, the initial 2027 commercial project remains focused on single-row FA 
using grating coupling (GC), while multi-row and multilayer configurations remain in 
sampling and are primarily associated with 2028 programs. Management believes 
its FA/FAU solution is broadly applicable to both CPO and NPO when the underlying 
optical interface remains similar, because the primary difference is the placement of 
the optical package. Largan’s primary differentiation is not the FA design itself but 
its ability to manufacture highly precise assembly using imperfect input 
components.
Automation and Yield Control Are the Real Competitive 
Advantages
During the earnings call, Largan’s management emphasized that almost all critical 
FA/FAU alignment equipment is developed internally, including machinery and 
control software. This enables faster equipment modification, process 
optimization and troubleshooting compared with labor-intensive assembly. 
Automated production also offers better traceability and root-cause analysis when 
yield problems emerge. Management stated that customer feedback is positive 
and the FAU certification process progressing well. The key competitive advantage, 
in our view, is the ability to combine submicron accuracy, high throughput and 
reproducible yields at scale, rather than precision alone. 
In our view, the earnings call supports a more constructive medium-term view of 
Largan’s CPO opportunities than our previous assessment, particularly given the 
apparent completion of initial FA qualification, customer interest in integrated FAU 
assembly and a clearer path toward commercial production in 2H27. Moving from 
standalone FA to FAU and potentially carrier assembly could materially increase 
revenue content per optical connection, while the company’s automated 
manufacturing capabilities may support differentiation in increasingly complex, 
high-density optical architectures. The next growth opportunity could emerge from 
multi-row FA and higher-channel-count optical solutions beginning in 2028, 
particularly as AI networking bandwidth moves beyond current-generation 
platforms.
Maintaining Buy on better FAU visibility 
Given the weak smartphone order flow and GM pressure in the near term, we revise 
down our net income projections by 9%/29% for 2026/2027, but slightly raise our 
2028 net income projection by 1% given the solid growth opportunity in FAU 
business. However, we think Largan is transitioning from a smartphone optics 
manufacturer into a potential high-precision optical interconnect assembly 
supplier. As they are moving to FAU not just FA; we assume higher revenue 
contribution for 2027 /2028 of 28%/ 44% considering Largan could get 15%/30% 
market share.

Largan Precision
Company description
Largan is a plastic/glass/hybrid lens supplier in Taiwan with end-applications 
including phone cameras, DSCs, MFPs, and tablets. Its new development into 
FAU business should server as a long term growth opportunity.
Investment strategy
We rate Largan a Buy as we expect its core iPhone business to remain resilient 
and its co-packaged optics (CPO) development to provide strong upside 
potential in the longer term. We believe Largan could be a long-term winner in 
the lens market driven by: 1) its technology leadership; 2) intellectual property 
(IP) protection; and 3) higher yield vs. competitors. In the longer term, we 
believe spec migration could keep Largan ahead of competitors.
Valuation
Our target price of NT$8,500 for Largan shares is based on 33x 2027 /28E 
EPS. We are using 2027 /28E EPS average as we see new Fiber Array + PMLA 
revenue to kick in from next year. Our 33x PER is higher than its historical 5-
year PER range, which we think is justified by its better order visibility proven 
by its recent strong capacity expansion plan, and we expect its CPO business 
engagement should provide a strong long-term growth opportunity.
Risks
Key downside risks include: 1) weaker smartphone demand or replacement 
demand, and in particular, demand headwinds for certain key clients; 2) 
longer learning curve and slower ramp of the yield rate; 3) slower spec 
migration; and 4) slower development in CPO business. Any of these risk 
factors could cause the shares to deviate from our target price.

Largan Precision (3008.TW)
Better FAU visibility despite smartphone shortfall
CITI'S TAKE
Largan’s 3Q26 earning was below expectation. 3Q26 revenue of
NT$15.65bn (up 15% QoQ but down 11% YoY). GM declined to 42.2% with
EPS reaching NT$39.6. Management attributed margin pressure to
manufacturing yield challenges associated with increasingly complicated
smartphone lenses, alongside the rising cost of renewable electricity. The
latter is becoming a structural cost burden because of contractual
commitments to customers. While yields are gradually improving,
management see weakening smartphone order flow into 4Q26.
Nevertheless, the management’s view on FAU development is positive
and seeing great feedback and strong business engagement into the next
generation CPO design. We reiterate our Buy and see any pull back on weak
smartphone business as a great buying opportunity.
CPO Strategy — Moving to integrated FAU and carrier assembly — The most
important development during the call is Largan’s expanded product scope.
Previously, the company primarily targeted Fiber Array alignment, positioning itself
as a high-precision component supplier to established FAU manufacturers.
Management now plans to produce FAU, purchase PMLA and other optical
components, and perform precision optical coupling and assembly to deliver
complete FAUs. It also intends to pursue the additional assembly step of mounting
the FAU onto a carrier, which subsequently interfaces with the receptacle. This
represents a meaningful expansion in value capture, moving Largan to higher-value
integrated optical interconnect assemblies.
Customer qualification has progressed well, production starting in mid-2027 —
Largan indicated that FA qualification is complete, and the automated pilot line is
already operational and has been inspected repeatedly by the customer. Largan
currently has one customer progressing toward commercial volume production,
while several other customers, including CSP-related opportunities, are involved in
next-generation development targeting 2028. Management expects the first scaled
production lines to be ready around mid-2027, with meaningful FAU mass
production potentially beginning in 2H27. Management also confirmed that recently
acquired land and facilities have designated expansion purposes, primarily
cleanrooms and production lines for FA/FAU rather than smartphone lenses.

Largan Precision (3008.TW)

Seeing multiple generation and years opportunities — Compared with these
broader solutions providers, Largan remains primarily as a high-precision
manufacturing and assembly specialist. Management described its current
business relationship as closer to contract manufacturing, with direct discussions
with end customers focused mainly on next-generation products. On product
architecture, the initial 2027 commercial project remains focused on single-row FA
using grating coupling (GC), while multi-row and multilayer configurations remain in
sampling and are primarily associated with 2028 programs. Management believes
its FA/FAU solution is broadly applicable to both CPO and NPO when the underlying
optical interface remains similar, because the primary difference is the placement of
the optical package. Largan’s primary differentiation is not the FA design itself but
its ability to manufacture highly precise assembly using imperfect input
components.
Automation and Yield Control Are the Real Competitive
Advantages
During the earnings call, Largan’s management emphasized that almost all critical
FA/FAU alignment equipment is developed internally, including machinery and
control software. This enables faster equipment modification, process
optimization and troubleshooting compared with labor-intensive assembly.
Automated production also offers better traceability and root-cause analysis when
yield problems emerge. Management stated that customer feedback is positive
and the FAU certification process progressing well. The key competitive advantage,
in our view, is the ability to combine submicron accuracy, high throughput and
reproducible yields at scale, rather than precision alone.
In our view, the earnings call supports a more constructive medium-term view of
Largan’s CPO opportunities than our previous assessment, particularly given the
apparent completion of initial FA qualification, customer interest in integrated FAU
assembly and a clearer path toward commercial production in 2H27. Moving from
standalone FA to FAU and potentially carrier assembly could materially increase
revenue content per optical connection, while the company’s automated
manufacturing capabilities may support differentiation in increasingly complex,
high-density optical architectures. The next growth opportunity could emerge from
multi-row FA and higher-channel-count optical solutions beginning in 2028,
particularly as AI networking bandwidth moves beyond current-generation
platforms.
Maintaining Buy on better FAU visibility
Given the weak smartphone order flow and GM pressure in the near term, we revise
down our net income projections by 9%/29% for 2026/2027, but slightly raise our
2028 net income projection by 1% given the solid growth opportunity in FAU
business. However, we think Largan is transitioning from a smartphone optics
manufacturer into a potential high-precision optical interconnect assembly
supplier. As they are moving to FAU not just FA; we assume higher revenue
contribution for 2027 /2028 of 28%/ 44% considering Largan could get 15%/30%
market share.

Largan Precision
Company description
Largan is a plastic/glass/hybrid lens supplier in Taiwan with end-applications
including phone cameras, DSCs, MFPs, and tablets. Its new development into
FAU business should server as a long term growth opportunity.
Investment strategy
We rate Largan a Buy as we expect its core iPhone business to remain resilient
and its co-packaged optics (CPO) development to provide strong upside
potential in the longer term. We believe Largan could be a long-term winner in
the lens market driven by: 1) its technology leadership; 2) intellectual property
(IP) protection; and 3) higher yield vs. competitors. In the longer term, we
believe spec migration could keep Largan ahead of competitors.
Valuation
Our target price of NT$8,500 for Largan shares is based on 33x 2027 /28E
EPS. We are using 2027 /28E EPS average as we see new Fiber Array + PMLA
revenue to kick in from next year. Our 33x PER is higher than its historical 5-
year PER range, which we think is justified by its better order visibility proven
by its recent strong capacity expansion plan, and we expect its CPO business
engagement should provide a strong long-term growth opportunity.
Risks
Key downside risks include: 1) weaker smartphone demand or replacement
demand, and in particular, demand headwinds for certain key clients; 2)
longer learning curve and slower ramp of the yield rate; 3) slower spec
migration; and 4) slower development in CPO business. Any of these risk
factors could cause the shares to deviate from our target price.

items.full_text:
【Raw_Inbox row21086】
🔥凱基投顧 劉昃恩 (Jenny)
 
⭐️即時資訊_營收公告—鋼鐵產業9月營收
 
2026/10/12
 
💎訊息內容
 
鋼鐵產業9月營收－普遍改善，主因天氣惡劣干擾因素排除，外銷追趕前月遞延出貨。中國金九銀十旺季不旺，原物料價格反轉下跌。
 
💎評論及分析
 
1. 中鋼 (2002 TT) 9月營收年增27%、月增11%至310億元；其中，鋼鐵產品年增30%，反映極端天氣與豪雨干擾因素消除，外銷裝船出貨轉順暢，非鐵工業材料及其他業務則分別年增43%、年減1%。3Q26營收年增21%、季持平至886.7億元，分別達成凱基預估93%、市場共識100%。

2. 中鴻 (2014 TT) 9月營收年減5%、但月增48%至15.1億元。3Q26營收年減8%、季減35%至37.9億元，僅分別達成凱基預估78%、市場共識79%。

3. 豐興 (2015 TT) 9月營收年減4%、月減9%至21.0億元。3Q26營收年增4%、但月減9%至68.8億元，達成市場共識99%。

4. 東鋼 (2006 TT) 9月營收年增14%、月增3%至54.2億元。3Q26營收年增14%、但季減3%至158.5億元，達成市場共識104%。

5. 歐美及亞洲鋼價走勢持續分化。由於各項貿易保護措施圍堵亞洲鋼品進口，美國及歐洲9月熱軋鋼價分別上漲6%、3%至1,375、850美元/噸。亞洲方面，中國金九銀十呈旺季不旺格局，9月熱軋鋼價下跌1%；再加上鐵礦砂及焦煤價格反轉下跌，成本支撐減弱抑制亞洲他國鋼價反彈幅度。台灣、韓國、日本、東南亞及印度熱軋現價分別落在609、676、565、533、518美元/噸。

6. 目前凱基給予中鋼、中鴻「持有」評等，目標價分別為20.3、18.6元。

【僅供內部參考，請勿外傳】

5. 歐美及亞洲鋼價走勢持續分化。由於各項貿易保護措施圍堵亞洲鋼品進口，美國及歐洲9月熱軋鋼價分別上漲6%、3%至1,375、850美元/噸。亞洲方面，中國金九銀十呈旺季不旺格局，9月熱軋鋼價下跌1%；再加上鐵礦砂及焦煤價格反轉下跌，成本支撐減弱抑制亞洲他國鋼價反彈幅度。台灣、韓國、日本、東南亞及印度熱軋現價分別落在609、676、565、533、518美元/噸。

6. 目前凱基給予中鋼、中鴻「持有」評等，目標價分別為20.3、18.6元。

Mizuho 
半導體與半導體資本設備｜光學供應鏈（InP/SiPho）：供應端深度分析 - 第二部分）

1.  InP 基板仍是最緊繃的瓶頸，Sumitomo/AXT 控制約 85% 的供應。

2.  估計 InP 基板產能在 2026E/2027E 成長 81%/32%，2028E 成長 34%，並有亞洲新產能加入。

3.  EML 是近期主力，LITE 持有約 33% 市占，以及約 50% 的高速 EML。

4.  CW 雷射產能從 2025 年約 8300 萬顆擴至 2029E 約 4.27 億顆（55% 滲透率），由可插拔模組/NPO/CPO 驅動，LITE/AVGO 在超高功率（UHP）CW 領先，總 CW 市占成長至約 20%/23%（2029E）。

5.  磊晶仍至關重要，IQE 與 LandMark 是領先的外部供應商。

【引用原文 @pequityresearch】
Mizuho: InP Supply 

> InP Substrate Bottleneck: InP substrate remains the tightest bottleneck in the supply chain, with Sumitomo Electric and AXT controlling approximately 85% of the market.

> Capacity Growth: Global InP substrate capacity is projected to grow significantly by 81% in 2026, 32% in 2027, and 34% in 2028, driven heavily by surging AI data center (DC) demand and increased optical bandwidth content.

> EML and Laser Trends: EML serves as the near-term workhorse, with LITE holding ~33% overall share and roughly 50% of high-speed EML. Meanwhile, CW laser capacity is scaling rapidly from ~83M units in 2025 to ~427M units by 2029.

> Epitaxy Providers: Epitaxy remains critical to the ecosystem, with IQE and LandMark acting as the leading external providers.

$LITE $CRDO $COHR $AXTI

items.story: UBS首次評等精測Buy,TP 5,000元;營業利益率24.8%(2025)升至35.3%/41.5%,2027-28營收預估高於共識7%/15%。
items.full_text:
【Raw_Inbox row20991】
(emoji)UBS_精測(6510, Initiate at Buy, TP$5,000)
 
(emoji)中華精測是晶圓級測試、成品測試、系統級測試及老化測試所需探針卡、探針卡PCB及介面板的主要供應商之一，也是少數具備先進AI/HPC應用高層數PCB製造能力的廠商，受惠於測試需求增加及產業產能吃緊。
 
(emoji)隨著高附加價值AI/HPC產品營收占比提升，加上垂直整合的製造模式，預期將帶動顯著的營運槓桿，營業利益率可望由2025年的24.8%提升至2026年及2027年的35.3%及41.5%，營收則預估分別成長49%及75%。目前股價對應2027年及2028年預估本益比分別僅24倍及16倍，低於公司及同業歷史近12個月本益比的31倍及30倍，後續應關注第三季法說會中管理層對2027年營運展望的說明。
 
(emoji)隨著產業逐步採用shift-left testing策略，更多測試程序將提前至封裝前的晶圓階段進行，且晶圓測試時間也將延長。在先進封裝成本持續上升的情況下，晶圓級測試的重要性進一步提高，預期將帶動探針卡及先進測試介面的長期需求。認為市場低估了此一趨勢，因此2027年及2028年營收預估分別高於市場共識7%及15%，主要受惠於AI/HPC結構性需求、產能擴充及單顆晶片測試價值提升。
 
(emoji)除了GPU，精測也逐步切入新興CPU及TPU商機。在CPU方面，公司有望供應NVIDIA Vera CPU及Google Axion CPU所需的探針卡與測試PCB，尤其在Axion CPU領域具備較強的市占率。預估CPU相關營收占比將由2026年的mid-teens提升至2027年的20%至30%。在TPU方面，預期公司將供應Google TPU v8t所需的探針卡PCB、final test load boards、system-level test boards及burn-in boards，並持續參與TPU v9的非晶圓測試介面業務，尤其受惠於聯發科在TPU供應鏈中的市占率提升。結合持續擴產，預估2026至2028年營收將分別成長49%、75%及43%。
 
(emoji)估2026/2027/2028年EPS 62.55/124.68/189.01元。

【Raw_Inbox row21130】
🔥凱基投顧  莊政翰 (Angus) 

⭐️即時資訊_營收公告— 美利達 (9914 TT)
 
2026/10/12
 
💎訊息內容
 
美利達 (9914 TT) 9月營收年減26%至16.9億元，明顯低於預期。
 
💎結論
 
1. 美利達九月份營收16.9億元，月減14%、年減26%。3Q26營收總計61.1億元，季減11%、年減16%，分別低於市場共識與凱基預估13%及6%，明顯低於預期。

2. 儘管中國市場受惠入門與登山車款需求回溫，銷量年增6%，但平均銷售單價衰退8%，營收僅年增4%。台灣廠受新舊車款過渡期影響，整體出貨量月減4%、年減21%至2.6萬輛，其中電動車出貨量大幅衰退，九月份僅6千台，月減45%、年減55%。

3. 由於台灣廠出口歐美市場新年度車款預計將於4Q26陸續開始出貨，我們認為4Q26營收有機會重回年增軌道，優於我們原估年減10%。

4. 隨著歐洲及中國市場需求回溫，我們預期新年度車款出貨及銷售單價復甦將帶動美利達明年獲利顯著年增。我們維持「增加持股」評等及目標價104元，係根據18倍本益比。

【僅供內部參考，請勿外傳】

3. 由於台灣廠出口歐美市場新年度車款預計將於4Q26陸續開始出貨，我們認為4Q26營收有機會重回年增軌道，優於我們原估年減10%。

4. 隨著歐洲及中國市場需求回溫，我們預期新年度車款出貨及銷售單價復甦將帶動美利達明年獲利顯著年增。我們維持「增加持股」評等及目標價104元，係根據18倍本益比。

Unimicron 
 
Extending capacity plan for ABF substrate 
and better margins in PCB/HDI; Buy 
 
Reiterate Rating: BUY | PO: 1,650 TWD | Price: 1,270 TWD    
 
  
  
  
   
 
   
 
Raise PO along with the hike in estimates 
We raise 2026/27/28E EPS by 5%/12%/10% after baking in a strengthened margin 
profile, partly thanks to further improved GM (gross margin) in PCB (printed circuit 
board) and HDI (high density interconnect) business. Our PO goes to NT$1,650 (was 
NT$1,400) same based on 35x 2H27-1H28E P/E. Reiterate Buy on Unimicron in view of 
its structurally growing exposure to AI-related (artificial intelligence) products, which in 
turn bolsters its GM profile in longer-term. 
Land acquisition to back long-term capacity growth  
Unimicron announced that it bought a land/building located in Hukuo (Hsinchu) from 
Bridgestone Taiwan, with the amount of NT$10.1bn. Our check with the company 
suggests that such property will be used for further capacity expansion beyond its YM 
(Yangmei) site, but the timing for output will only take place in 2030 at earliest. Of note, 
the company will expand 30+% of its ABF (Ajinomoto build-up film) capacity in 2027 via 
the KF2 (KuangFu 2) plant, and there will be YM3 capacity coming on stream in 2029 
after the expansion YM2 in 2028 backed by 5-year LTA (long-term agreement). For 
2027/28 capex, currently we expect to reach NT$40+bn each year. 
Rosier margin outlook in PCB/HDI business  
Unimicron is one of the major (if not biggest) PCB suppliers to high-end (see report) 
optical module, where demand growth is expected to remain robust coupled with spec 
upgrades in the upcoming years. Management cites such business carries 30+% GM 
currently, while the number by AI HDI in China production lines is moving closer to peers’ 
level. Yet, the PCB/HDI lines in Taiwan still carry lower GM. Currently, we assume its GM 
in HDI business to reach 20+% from mid-2027, along with the continuous yield/output 
improvements.

Company Sector 
Electronics 
  
Company Description 
Unimicron (3037 TT) was founded in 1990 and listed on 
the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 1998. The firm manufactures 
a wide range of PCB and IC substrates for consumer 
electronics, industrial, and automotive. It is also the leading 
ABF supplier globally. The company merged with Phoenix 
Precision Technology (PPT, delisted) in 2009 and expanded 
its exposure in the IC substrate business. UMC is the 
biggest shareholder in Unimicron with a 13.3% stake. 
 
Investment Rationale 
We have a Buy rating on Unimicron in view of strong 
demand from AI accelerators (especially ASICs), which we 
expect to boost the utilization rate of the ABF substrate 
business from 2H26, in turn bolstering the company's 
margin profile and profitability going into 2027.

Price objective basis & risk 
Unimicron (UMCRF) 
Our PO of NT$1,650 is based on 35x 2H27-1H28E, which is roughly 1 standard deviation 
above the historical average of 20x since 2017. In our view, the multiple is appropriate, 
as we expect Unimicron's earnings to be supported by its high-end technology offerings, 
where end market demand seems more resilient. 
 
Upside risks are (1) tighter ABF supply, (2) greater PC and regular server demand, and (3) 
lower competition pressure. 
 
Downside risks are (1) greater ABF expansion from peers, (2) lower ASP content increase 
at AI server, and (3) bigger drop in the demand of consumer electronic products.

Unimicron

Extending capacity plan for ABF substrate
and better margins in PCB/HDI; Buy

Reiterate Rating: BUY | PO: 1,650 TWD | Price: 1,270 TWD

Raise PO along with the hike in estimates
We raise 2026/27/28E EPS by 5%/12%/10% after baking in a strengthened margin
profile, partly thanks to further improved GM (gross margin) in PCB (printed circuit
board) and HDI (high density interconnect) business. Our PO goes to NT$1,650 (was
NT$1,400) same based on 35x 2H27-1H28E P/E. Reiterate Buy on Unimicron in view of
its structurally growing exposure to AI-related (artificial intelligence) products, which in
turn bolsters its GM profile in longer-term.
Land acquisition to back long-term capacity growth
Unimicron announced that it bought a land/building located in Hukuo (Hsinchu) from
Bridgestone Taiwan, with the amount of NT$10.1bn. Our check with the company
suggests that such property will be used for further capacity expansion beyond its YM
(Yangmei) site, but the timing for output will only take place in 2030 at earliest. Of note,
the company will expand 30+% of its ABF (Ajinomoto build-up film) capacity in 2027 via
the KF2 (KuangFu 2) plant, and there will be YM3 capacity coming on stream in 2029
after the expansion YM2 in 2028 backed by 5-year LTA (long-term agreement). For
2027/28 capex, currently we expect to reach NT$40+bn each year.
Rosier margin outlook in PCB/HDI business
Unimicron is one of the major (if not biggest) PCB suppliers to high-end (see report)
optical module, where demand growth is expected to remain robust coupled with spec
upgrades in the upcoming years. Management cites such business carries 30+% GM
currently, while the number by AI HDI in China production lines is moving closer to peers’
level. Yet, the PCB/HDI lines in Taiwan still carry lower GM. Currently, we assume its GM
in HDI business to reach 20+% from mid-2027, along with the continuous yield/output
improvements.

Company Sector
Electronics

Company Description
Unimicron (3037 TT) was founded in 1990 and listed on
the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 1998. The firm manufactures
a wide range of PCB and IC substrates for consumer
electronics, industrial, and automotive. It is also the leading
ABF supplier globally. The company merged with Phoenix
Precision Technology (PPT, delisted) in 2009 and expanded
its exposure in the IC substrate business. UMC is the
biggest shareholder in Unimicron with a 13.3% stake.

Investment Rationale
We have a Buy rating on Unimicron in view of strong
demand from AI accelerators (especially ASICs), which we
expect to boost the utilization rate of the ABF substrate
business from 2H26, in turn bolstering the company's
margin profile and profitability going into 2027.

Price objective basis & risk
Unimicron (UMCRF)
Our PO of NT$1,650 is based on 35x 2H27-1H28E, which is roughly 1 standard deviation
above the historical average of 20x since 2017. In our view, the multiple is appropriate,
as we expect Unimicron's earnings to be supported by its high-end technology offerings,
where end market demand seems more resilient.

Upside risks are (1) tighter ABF supply, (2) greater PC and regular server demand, and (3)
lower competition pressure.

Downside risks are (1) greater ABF expansion from peers, (2) lower ASP content increase
at AI server, and (3) bigger drop in the demand of consumer electronic products.
